title: Let marketing move a campaign to any week

blocks.text: The shop's front page runs sale campaigns, and marketing moves them around the calendar. This morning they tried to move the autumn sale from 11–15 October to 25–29 October, and the admin screen refused it, although the new week is a perfectly good campaign.

`Campaign` keeps a first and a last day, both included, and a campaign never ends before it starts. Its constructor, getters and `setStartsOn` are written. Finish the two `TODO`s in `src/main/java/practice/Campaign.java`:

items: `setEndsOn(...)`: change the last day of a running campaign;
`moveTo(...)`: move the campaign to a new window.

blocks.text: When you're done, a campaign can be moved from any valid window to any other valid window, and a date or a window the campaign refuses leaves it exactly as it was. About eight lines in total.

cases.says: a campaign can be extended, moved within its own dates and shrunk to one day
a move or a last day that would end the campaign before it starts is refused with IllegalArgumentException
a campaign moves to a week that starts after its current last day
a campaign moves to a week that ends before its current first day
after a refused move the campaign keeps both of its old dates
after a refused last day the campaign keeps its old last day

origin.section: A Setter Can Check Its Own Value, Not a Rule That Spans Two Fields

concepts: A method that checks every argument before it assigns any field leaves the object unchanged when it refuses; one that assigns first leaves half a change behind.
A setter can compare its value only with the fields as they are now, so a rule over two fields set one at a time refuses some valid changes, and it needs one method that takes both values.
